blueprint_topic: Management of Care — early multidisciplinary rehabilitation assessment and specialist spinal-cord-injury input after traumatic injury
stem: A client with a new traumatic spinal cord injury is entering rehabilitation. Which plan best reflects a person-centered multidisciplinary approach to rehabilitation?

options.A: Assess physical, cognitive, and psychological needs early with the multidisciplinary team, and obtain specialist spinal-cord-injury input for the plan.
options.B: Prioritize mobility and self-care first, adding cognitive and psychological review later if those concerns begin to interfere with rehabilitation.
options.C: Use the physical therapist's functional assessment as the main rehabilitation baseline, adding other disciplines after mobility goals have been established.
options.D: Set long-term functional targets from initial neurologic findings, then use later multidisciplinary reviews mainly to measure progress toward those targets.

rationale: A is correct. Current NICE guideline NG211 recommends that the multidisciplinary team complete a personalized, holistic rehabilitation-needs assessment in partnership with the person and family or carers as appropriate, including physical, cognitive, and psychological functioning. NICE also recommends specialist assessment for spinal injuries and assessment of rehabilitation needs as soon as possible after traumatic injury. The guideline cautions that long-term prognosis can be difficult to predict and should be discussed after multidisciplinary review rather than treated as certain from early findings. NCSBN places multidisciplinary collaboration and referral assessment within Management of Care. B is incorrect because it delays cognitive and psychological assessment even though NICE includes both domains in the initial holistic assessment. C is incorrect because a physical-therapy assessment is valuable but should not substitute for multidisciplinary assessment of the broader rehabilitation needs. D is incorrect because early neurologic findings should not be used to lock in long-term functional targets with unwarranted prognostic certainty; goals and needs should be informed by multidisciplinary review and reassessment.
educational_objective: Coordinate traumatic spinal-cord-injury rehabilitation through early, person-centered multidisciplinary assessment of physical, cognitive, and psychological needs with specialist spinal-injury input when indicated.
source_organization: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE); National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
source_document_title: Rehabilitation after traumatic injury (NG211) — Recommendations; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
source_version_date: NICE NG211 published 2022-01-18 and current recommendations rechecked 2026-08-20; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective April 2026
source_locator: NICE NG211 current Recommendations: 1.1.1 recommends a person-centred, individualised and holistic approach at all stages; 1.2.1 requires a personalised holistic multidisciplinary rehabilitation-needs assessment including physical, cognitive, and psychological functioning; 1.2.2 requires additional specialist assessments for spinal injuries; 1.2.5 says rehabilitation needs should be assessed as soon as possible after traumatic injury; 1.2.9 requires detailed analysis of injuries, impairments, goals and likely rehabilitation needs and discussion of findings together; 1.2.10 states long-term prognosis may be difficult to predict and should be discussed only after multidisciplinary-team review. NICE section 1.15 additionally supports specialist spinal-cord-injury input, but UK-specific referral infrastructure and database timing are intentionally not imported into this NCLEX item. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan Management of Care supports multidisciplinary collaboration, referral assessment, plan-of-care coordination, and resource use.
source_claim_supported: Current NICE guidance directly supports early, individualized multidisciplinary rehabilitation assessment across physical, cognitive, and psychological domains and specialist assessment/input for spinal injury. NCSBN supports the nursing coordination/referral construct. The final item intentionally generalizes the clinical principle and does not assert UK-specific referral systems as U.S. nursing requirements.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, assess need for referrals, initiate/evaluate/update the plan of care, and utilize resources to promote quality client care.

correction_summary: Original Q1973 had a 171-character correct answer, much shorter distractors, an absolute-word cue, and alternatives that caricatured multidisciplinary rehabilitation. The item was rebuilt so B/C/D are realistic sequencing or prognostic errors rather than denials of rehabilitation. UK-specific NICE infrastructure such as national-database referral timing was deliberately excluded; the item retains only portable clinical principles supported by current NICE guidance and NCSBN Management of Care. Independent post-fetch reread found no unresolved source, currentness, portability, rehabilitation-scope, ambiguity, cueing, blueprint, or second-answer conflict.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches early holistic multidisciplinary assessment across physical, cognitive, and psychological domains plus specialist spinal-injury input.
option_audit.B: Plausible mobility-first sequencing error; incorrect because NICE includes cognitive and psychological domains in the holistic assessment rather than waiting until they disrupt therapy.
option_audit.C: Plausible PT-led baseline approach; incorrect because one discipline's functional assessment cannot substitute for the broader multidisciplinary rehabilitation-needs assessment.
option_audit.D: Plausible goal-setting overreach; incorrect because long-term prognosis can be difficult to predict and early findings should not be treated as sufficient to lock in long-term targets without multidisciplinary review.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on all/only/always/never/must-type absolute wording.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final option lengths: A 151, B 146, C 156, D 156 characters; the correct answer is not the longest and choices are tightly balanced.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives describe plausible rehabilitation-planning strategies and differ in assessment breadth, sequencing, or prognostic certainty.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: Independent adversarial reread found no defensible second answer. B delays required assessment domains, C substitutes a single discipline for multidisciplinary assessment, and D overstates early prognostic certainty; A is uniquely aligned with current guidance.

The item does not import UK-specific database/referral timing and does not claim that one discipline or early neurologic findings can substitute for multidisciplinary assessment.
